title: NY State Senate · District 13
area: Central Queens, including Jackson Heights, East Elmhurst, Corona and parts of Woodside and Elmhurst.

context.text: Incumbent Jessica Ramos lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. State Assemblymember Jessica González-Rojas won the primary with 47.9% of the vote (6,476 votes) against Ramos's 37.1% (5,024 votes) and Hiram Monserrate's 14.5% (1,966 votes); Ramos does not appear on the November general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Jessica González-Rojas
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assemblymember, District 34 (since 2021; not seeking re-election to the Assembly)

summary.text: Jessica González-Rojas is a NY State Assemblymember (District 34, Queens) running for the open NY State Senate District 13 seat after defeating incumbent Jessica Ramos in the June 2026 Democratic primary. Before her 2020 election to the Assembly she spent more than 13 years at the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice, including as Executive Director, and she has also taught as an adjunct professor. She chairs the Assembly's Task Force on Women's Issues and has said she is running on healthcare access and protecting immigrant communities.

background.text: Born and lives in Queens, New York; her Assembly biography says she lives in Jackson Heights with her partner and son.

Earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Boston University (graduating cum laude) and a master's degree from the NYU Wagner Graduate School of Public Service, with a concentration in public and nonprofit management and public policy; also holds a nonprofit management certificate from Columbia Business School's Executive Leadership Program.

Served in leadership for more than 13 years at the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice (formerly the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Health), including as Executive Director, before running for office.

Has taught as an adjunct professor at the NYU Wagner Graduate School of Public Service and CUNY's City College, and is an Adjunct Clinical Professor at the NYU School of Law, according to her Assembly biography.

In her 2020 Ballotpedia candidate survey she described herself as a community organizer, a founding board member of New Immigrant Community Empowerment (NICE) in Jackson Heights, and a co-founder of the New Visions Democratic Club; she says that in 2002 she became the first Latina to represent her community on the Democratic Party's State Committee.

Won the June 23, 2020 Democratic primary for Assembly District 34, defeating incumbent Michael DenDekker and three other candidates, then won the November 2020 general election over William Marquez; took office in 2021 as the first person of color, woman of color and Latina to represent the district, according to her Assembly welcome letter. Re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Serves on the Assembly's Children and Families, Cities, Corporations Authorities and Commissions, Environmental Conservation, Health, and Social Services committees (2025-2026 session), and was appointed Chair of the Task Force on Women's Issues for 2025-2026. Her official biography also lists her as Chair of the Subcommittee on Human Trafficking and Board Secretary of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic, and Asian Legislative Caucus.

Her official biography credits her as prime sponsor of the Universal School Meals Act and says she secured $25 million in the 2024 state budget to codify the Reproductive Freedom and Equity Fund, and was a champion of Sammy's Law.

Serves as Northeast Region Chair on the board of the National Hispanic Caucus of State Legislators and on the board of If/When/How, a national reproductive-justice nonprofit network of law students and lawyers.

positions.summary: Supports the New York Health Act (a state version of Medicare for All) to guarantee healthcare regardless of income, employment or immigration status.
Says she is running to protect immigrant communities and make New York a sanctuary state, and to secure relief for immigrants excluded from federal aid.

record.text: Appointed Chair of the NY State Assembly's Task Force on Women's Issues by Speaker Carl Heastie for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the Assembly's Children and Families, Cities, Corporations Authorities and Commissions, Environmental Conservation, Health, and Social Services committees (2025-2026 session).

summary.text: John Healy is the Republican candidate for the open NY State Senate District 13 seat. A Queens native and President of the Sunnyside GOP Club, he ran for NYC Council District 26 in 2025 on the Republican and Conservative lines and lost to incumbent Julie Won. Little other biographical detail is publicly available.

background.text: A Queens native who, as of the New York Young Republican Club's March 2025 endorsement, served as President of the Sunnyside GOP Club.

Ran for New York City Council District 26 (Western Queens) in 2025 on the Republican and Conservative Party lines; lost the November 4, 2025 general election to incumbent Julie Won, receiving 18.3% (7,498 votes) to her 81.4% (33,425 votes).
Is on the November 3, 2026 ballot as the Republican candidate for State Senate District 13; the June 23, 2026 Republican primary was canceled and he advanced without appearing on the ballot.

priorities.text: In his prior Council campaign, an endorsing club described his focus on Western Queens quality-of-life issues, including "safer and cleaner streets, improved quality of life, and preservation of the character of our communities."
priorities.quote: safer and cleaner streets, improved quality of life, and preservation of the character of our communities

researchNotes: John Healy has no known campaign website or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection response for this race (re-checked https://ballotpedia.org/John_Healy on 2026-09-25: no Biography section, and he has not completed the 2026 or 2025 Candidate Connection surveys). The sourced background and priorities here come from a New York Young Republican Club endorsement of his overlapping 2025 NYC Council campaign (nyyrc.com), the only substantive record of his positions found; no statements addressing the guide's 15 fixed issue keys were found, so no `positions` entries were added. Jessica González-Rojas's priorities in the current Senate race could not be independently verified beyond her 2020 Ballotpedia candidate survey answers (still displayed on her current Ballotpedia page) and her official Assembly bio; a July 2026 Spectrum News item covering her Senate primary win was video-only and its text did not describe specific policy priorities, so it was removed as a source. Biography details for Jessica González-Rojas come from her official Assembly biography and her Ballotpedia profile; John Healy's biography is limited to the 2025 endorsement and Ballotpedia pages cited, as no campaign biography page could be loaded.
